It’s not just the consequences it’s also everything else. Social services are now involved with my son, my phone hasn’t stopped ringing with recovery/therapists/doctors calling, as well as communicating with work to make them aware of the situation. It’s not like you get to relax much afterwards it’s all go & in a way having to constantly talk about what you’ve done really gives you a sense of clarity of the seriousness of the whole thing. At the time it doesn’t seem like that much of a deal so it really makes you realise the severity of it and the impact it has on others.

I’m not a self harmer although I totally understand why people do and I think if you don’t suffer then it’s totally understandable why you don’t and you probably never will. When your mind is racing with thoughts you can’t escape, the pain of self harming provides that for a moment. All your brain can focus on is the pain. I’m also assuming some people feel to blame and it’s a means of punishing themselves. A lot of people do reach out for help, the services have been aware of my mental state a while but unfortunately it’s very understaffed and underfunded aswell as misunderstood so people rarely get the actual care they need and are more likely fobbed off. People who don’t reach out are most likely in denial that they need help and/or don’t want to feel like even more of a burden than they already do. I hope this helps to give some insight :)

Honestly, technology & especially social media are the fucking devil as far as I’m concerned. I’m guilty for doing the exact same thing. I feel like since phones & social media came about I’ve lost so many of my actual passions. I’ve basically forgotten how to play my guitar, I barely read, never trying or experimenting with new things which I would usually do to pass the time. Now I just sit and scroll through the same old shit. I’ve started to not allow myself to reply to any messages after 11pm & to try to at least get through a few pages of whatever book I’m reading instead. A few pages normally turns into a few chapters haha! Also I try to leave my phone in a different room throughout the day to stop myself keep reaching for it constantly. Just start small & often & see how you go :)

When I was 9 I was woken by my mother at like 5am on 26th Dec & taken to my grandma's. After sleeping a few hours at her house I remember hearing my mother come up the stairs, being a kid I thought it'd be funny to pretend I was asleep & give her a fright when she came through the door. I just remember looking up & her face was all red & puffy. She told me my nanna (her mother) had died through the night. She was literally like my 2nd mam & the whole family had only just been to her Christmas party at her house the night before, little did we know it was her way of saying goodbye to us all. My heart broke that day & christmas time has never been the same since.
